gaps.sentence: Not until the second edition ___ the book become a bestseller.
gaps.explanation: 'Not until the second edition did the book become …'.

gaps.sentence: At no time ___ the crew aware of the danger.
gaps.explanation: 'At no time was the crew aware' — inverted past simple of be.

gaps.sentence: Little did the suspects ___ that the police were listening.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did they know' — 'know' as bare verb after the inverted auxiliary 'did'.

gaps.sentence: Rarely ___ this metro line run this late.
gaps.explanation: Rarely at the front: does + subject + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: ___ the storm passed did the ferries resume service.
gaps.explanation: Only after/once the storm passed did… — fronted 'only' phrase.

gaps.sentence: ___ as it may sound, the machine still works perfectly.
gaps.explanation: Adjective + as + subject + verb = although it sounds strange.

gaps.sentence: Reluctant ___ she was to intervene, the referee stopped the match.
gaps.explanation: Fronted adjective + though/as + subject is emphatic concession: Reluctant though she was…

gaps.sentence: In no way ___ this report reflect the views of the editor.
gaps.explanation: In no way does this reflect… — formal disclaimer structure.
